prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which promotions started in June 2025? From the promotions table, return four columns, in this order: promo_code, promo_name, start_date, discount_pct. Keep only the promotions whose start_date is from 1 June 2025 to 30 June 2025, both days included. start_date is a date with no time of day, and every promotion has one. Show discount_pct exactly as stored, without rounding. Return one row per promotion. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the end of the date range: a promotion that started in June is missing from the rows the query returns.
The question includes both end days, so the end test must keep a promotion that started on 30 June. Look at the operator in front of the second date.
starter_sql:
SELECT promo_code, promo_name, start_date, discount_pct
FROM promotions
WHERE start_date >= DATE '2025-06-01' AND start_date < DATE '2025-06-30'
why_this_works: BETWEEN keeps both end days of a DATE range, so a promotion that started on 30 June counts; < 30 June left that day out.
